# Sigil

> Sigil turns an integer into one recognizable Cistercian-style glyph: a
> single vertical stem plus a small set of toggled line segments, one quadrant
> per digit place. Four digits is the historical default; the range is derived
> from the model, so a taller stem carries more digits as one mark. The number logic is ~150 lines with zero
> dependencies; output formats (SVG, ASCII, DXF, Canvas, font, audio, STL)
> are thin renderers over one segment list. One repo: the spec and the
> golden fixtures at the root, each language implementation beside them.

## Contract

- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): the full specification — data model, digit→segment
  table, quadrant transforms, encoder algorithm, renderer contract.
- [model.json](model.json): Tier 1, the declarative definition — segment
  shapes, digit map (as a seven-segment-style bitmask), quadrant transforms,
  default geometry. Every implementation loads this file; none retype it.
- [fixtures/vectors-wide.json](fixtures/vectors-wide.json): the same model at
  1, 3 and 4 rows -- what stops a port hardcoding four places.
- [fixtures/vectors.json](fixtures/vectors.json): Tier 2, the resolved output
  for 15 numbers, and the compliance check. An implementation is
  spec-compliant exactly when it reproduces these. Generated by
  `sigil-php/bin/vectors.php`; never hand-edited.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what to read, and what not to change, before
  writing an implementation.

## Implementations

- [sigil-php/](sigil-php): PHP, published as `laxit/sigil`. SVG, ASCII and
  DXF renderers. Working.
- `sigil-js/` (planned) — JS/TS; home of the Canvas renderer and a
  `<sigil-glyph value="1234">` web component.
- `sigil-py/` (planned) — Python, for server-side generation.
- `sigil-cli/` (planned) — single dependency-free binary, likely Go or Rust.

Each is self-contained with its own manifest, dependencies, tests and
AGENTS.md. Nothing is shared between them except fixtures/vectors.json.

## Key facts

- Default range is 0-9999 (2 rows, 4 places) -- the historical system. Not a
  geometric limit: rows are configurable, up to 18 places, and more rows make
  one taller mark rather than several glyphs.
- A language with a lower exact-integer ceiling than the spec's 18 places must
  refuse inexact input rather than approximate it: JS Numbers run out at 15
  places, so js-sigil takes number | bigint | string.
- The range is DERIVED as 10^count(places)-1, never declared. A declared range
  could contradict the places, and then 12345 would silently render as 2345.
- `0` is valid and renders as the bare stem.
- Model/renderer separation is enforced: renderers use
  `Encoder.segmentsFor()` and `Encoder.stem()` only, never `SegmentModel`
  or `Quadrant`.
- Changing model.json is a breaking change for every language implementation
  simultaneously; regenerate the fixtures in the same commit.
- model.json's `segments` array order is both the bit position in `digitMap`
  and the emit order — append only, never reorder.
- Fixtures cover 0-9 as bare digits (so every digit's mapping is tested
  directly), 10/100/1000 for the quadrant transforms, 7323/9999 composite.
- Implementations release independently (`php-v1.2.0`, `js-v0.3.1`);
  Packagist and friends are fed by read-only `git subtree split` mirrors.
